item.title: Simple Torsion-Free Linear Groups from Global Division Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.37703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the reduced norm-one group $\mathrm{SL}_1(D)$ of a central division algebra $D$ of odd degree over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using the Brauer-Hasse-Noether theorem and the Margulis-Platonov theorem, we derive a criterion for abstract simplicity in terms of local division completions. For a division algebra of degree $15$ with local invariants $1/3$, $-1/3$, $1/5$, and $-1/5$, the construction yields a candidate example of an infinite, torsion-free, nonabelian simple linear group. This would provide an affirmative answer to Problem 16.78 of the Kourovka Notebook. The argument was generated using an AI system and has not yet been independently verified by human mathematicians.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Samuil Nnuga Mongo

item.title: Quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products
item.description: arXiv:2610.37824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide obstructions to the existence of quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products of trees, hyperbolic spaces, and other right-angled Artin groups.
item.dc:creator: Shaked Bader, Oussama Bensaid, Harry Petyt

item.title: On isomorphisms of tetravalent Cayley graphs over generalized quaternion groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $S$ be a subset of $G$ with $1\not\in S$. $S$ is called a $CI$-subset of $G$ if for any $T\subset G$, whenever $Cay (G,S)\cong Cay (G,T)$, there is an element $\sigma\in Aut(G)$ such that $S^{\sigma}=T$. For a positive integer $m$, $G$ is called an $m$-$CI$-group if all subsets $S$ of $G \setminus \{1\}$ with $|S|\leq m$ and $S^{-1}=S$ are $CI$-subsets. In this paper, we show that the generalized quaternion group of order $4n$ is a $4$-$CI$-group if and only if $n$ is odd.
item.dc:creator: Lele Jin, Li Ma, Wei Meng

item.title: Transfer kernels and the Schur multiplier
item.description: arXiv:2610.38640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we prove that if $H$ is a normal subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $G/H$ cyclic, then the kernel of the transfer map $G/G' \longrightarrow H/H'$ equals $(G:H)$ times the order of the cokernel of the natural map $M(H) \longrightarrow M(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Franz Lemmermeyer

item.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups. Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a subgroup. A subgroup $F\le G$ is a supplement of $H$ in $G$ if $G=HF$. We prove that for $H\le G$ with $F$ a supplement of $H$ in $G$, for generating sets $A_H$ and $A_G$ of $H$ and $G$ satisfying certain conditions involving $F$, the Vietoris-Rips complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;A_G)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A_H)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$. In particular this applies to affine Coxeter groups, since free abelian groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. Beyond these general results, we also investigate affine Coxeter groups $W_a$ specifically using the standard generating set $S$, and prove contractibility of $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ for large enough $t$.
item.dc:creator: Riley Decker, Matthew C. B. Zaremsky

item.title: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chapman, Dinur, and Lubotzky recently introduced the theory of non-commutative error-correcting codes, generalizing classical coding theory to arbitrary groups via $\delta$-robust subsets used to detect proper subgroups. Building on this foundation, this paper systematically studies an analogue of random codes for arbitrary groups, exploring the extent to which the classical Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound holds in this non-commutative setting. While random universal codes of linear size in free groups are shown to be asymptotically bad, we establish a complete characterization for general families of finite groups. Specifically, a family of finite groups admits good random codes (forming a GV family) if and only if it exhibits uniform polynomial maximal-subgroup growth. Furthermore, we provide explicit quantitative bounds on the rate and optimal distance range based on intrinsic parameters, proving that families of finite solvable groups always form GV families and determining the exact probabilistic rate for direct powers of a fixed finite simple group.
item.dc:creator: Michael Best, Alexander Lubotzky

item.title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.38841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Alexey V. Naianzin, Andronick A. Arutyunov

item.title: Grothendieck Pairs, Functors and Profinite Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2610.38991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As another variation of profinite properties, we define the notion of natural profinite invariants: functorial invariants, inducing isomorphisms for every Grothendieck pair. We give a characterisation of when adjoint functors are natural profinite invariants and describe a strategy on how to disprove natural profinite invariance. By means of examples we show that the notions of profinite invariance and natural profinite invariances are logically independent.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Echtler

item.title: Complete regular dessins and non-metacyclic bicyclic 2-groups with cyclic commutator subgroup
item.description: arXiv:2610.39407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study complete regular dessins with underlying graph ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$, where $e\geq f\geq 2$, whose automorphism groups are non-metacyclic. Together with the cases of coprime orders and odd-prime-power orders, this is one of the basic classes needed for Jones's open classification problem for regular dessins of complete bipartite graphs. Within the 2-power case, the present paper treats the subcase in which the commutator subgroup is cyclic; it is the first of three papers devoted to the non-metacyclic case. Our approach is group-theoretic. The automorphism group $G$ of a regular dessin of ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$ admits an exact bicyclic factorization $G=\langle b\rangle\langle w\rangle$ of type $(2^e,2^f)$ with $\langle b\rangle\cap\langle w\rangle=1$. For a fixed group $G$, two exact generating pairs give isomorphic dessins exactly when they lie in the same orbit under ${\rm A}ut(G)$. Thus the classification reduces to three group-theoretic tasks: determining the isomorphism classes of the possible groups $G$, characterizing their exact bicyclic generating pairs, and computing $|{\rm A}ut(G)|$. Berkovich and Janko divided the relevant non-metacyclic groups, through parameterized presentations, according to whether the commutator subgroup is cyclic, contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2$, or contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2^r$ with $r>1$. However, their classification does not identify which parameter values in these presentations define isomorphic groups; this problem was raised by Janko in {J}. We carry out these steps for the cyclic-commutator case. This settles Janko's isomorphism-classification problem in this case and yields a complete classification and enumeration of the corresponding regular dessins.
item.dc:creator: Wenwen Fan, Yuan Shi, Yun Tian Wu

item.title: Subindices of two-element subsets of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.39463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be a nonempty subset of a group $G$. A right subfactor relative to $A$ is a subset $B$ maximal under inclusion among those for which every element of $AB$ has a unique representation as $ab$, with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. Left subfactors are defined analogously using $BA$. The infima and suprema of the cardinalities of right and left subfactors define four \emph{subindices}. A subset is called \emph{index-stable} if its four subindices coincide. For any infinite group $G$, every nonempty finite subset of $G$ is index-stable. For finite groups, the situation is more complicated. We prove that for a two-element subset of a finite group, the left and right subindices coincide pairwise. Let $A=\{x,y\}$ with $x\ne y$, and let $X$ be the cyclic subgroup generated by $x^{-1}y$. Then the lower subindex of $A$ is $|G:X|\cdot\lceil |X|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is $|G:X|\cdot\lfloor |X|/2\rfloor$. These formulas imply that $A$ is index-stable if and only if $|X|$ is one of $2,3,4,5,7$. For any two-element subset of a finite group $G$, the lower subindex is at least $\lceil |G|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is at most $\lfloor |G|/2\rfloor$. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in each of these bounds. All two-element subsets of a finite group are index-stable if and only if every element of the group has order $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $5$, or $7$. We give a complete structural classification of such groups.
item.dc:creator: M. H. Hooshmand, Mikhail Kabenyuk

item.title: Epimorphism testing with dihedral targets
item.description: arXiv:2610.39487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of deciding whether or not there is an epimorphism from the class of finitely presented groups to a fixed finite group. We show this problem is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete when the target is a non-nilpotent dihedral group. This complements work of Kuperberg and Samperton (2018, Geom. Topol.) who showed the same result when the target is a fixed finite non-abelian simple group. We also include a survey of complexity and reduction results when the source and target are classes of finitely presented groups.
item.dc:creator: Murray Elder, Jerry Shen, Armin Wei{\ss}

item.title: Random semigroups \'a la Gromov
item.description: arXiv:2610.39673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $\delta\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2\delta l}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $\delta<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.
item.dc:creator: Guy Blachar, Be'eri Greenfeld, Margaret Shideler

item.title: Large Ree groups acting point and line-primitively on finite generalised quadrangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.39690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose we have a finite thick generalised quadrangle whose automorphism group $G$ acts primitively on both the set of points and the set of lines. Then $G$ must be almost simple. Furthermore, $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 B_2(2^{2m+1})$ or ${}^2 G_2(3^{2m+1})$, where $m$ is a positive integer. In this paper, we show that $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 F_4(2^{2m+1})$.
item.dc:creator: Vishnuram Arumugam

item.title: On $\kappa$-existentially closed groups with few automorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.39700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give constructions of $\kappa$-existentially closed groups having few automorphisms, giving negative solutions to a question of Kaya and Kuzucuo\u{g}lu in the Kourovka Notebook.
item.dc:creator: Samuel M. Corson, Saharon Shelah

item.title: Discrete hermitian groups are FC-hypercentral
item.description: arXiv:2610.40226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a discrete group is hermitian if and only if it is FC-hypercentral, that is, if and only if it does not have any nontrivial ICC quotients. In particular, a finitely generated group is hermitian if and only if it is virtually nilpotent. The main step is an elementary, self-contained proof that every hermitian ICC group is trivial, based on a finite-set separation property of nontrivial ICC groups.
item.dc:creator: Tron Omland

item.title: Lie (super)algebras generated by reflections in finite reflection groups of exceptional type
item.description: arXiv:2610.37890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using a mixture of theoretical tools and computer calculations, we describe the Lie subalgebras and the Lie sub-superalgebras generated by the sets of reflections in the group algebras of the exceptional finite reflection groups.
item.dc:creator: Christopher M. Drupieski, Jonathan R. Kujawa

item.title: Maximal regular subsemigroups containing the group of units of transformation semigroups that preserve a uniform equivalence relation with two classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38341v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $E$ an equivalence relation on $X$. The semigroup $T_E(X)$ consists of all transformations on $X$ that preserve $E$. Although the collection of all regular elements of $T_E(X)$ is not, in general, a subsemigroup, we investigate maximal regular subsemigroups of $T_E(X)$ containing the group of units $G_E(X)$. We construct two such maximal regular subsemigroups, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$, and show that their maximality holds in full generality for an arbitrary set $X$ and an arbitrary equivalence relation $E$ that is neither the identity relation nor the universal relation on $X$ (whether finite or infinite, uniform or non-uniform). Furthermore, when $X$ is finite and $E$ is a uniform equivalence relation with exactly two classes of cardinality at least $2$, we provide a complete classification by proving that they are the only maximal regular subsemigroups containing $G_E(X)$.
item.dc:creator: Kritsada Sangkhanan

item.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
item.description: arXiv:2610.38760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.
item.dc:creator: Oren Ben-Bassat

item.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$. In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.
item.dc:creator: Timothy C. Burness, Tao Feng, Jianbing Lu

item.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.
item.dc:creator: Grant Barkley, Colin Defant, Patricia Hersh, Jon McCammond, Thomas McConville, David E Speyer

item.title: Invariant means, coset correct means and the Hahn-Banach Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, in ZF set theory, the existence of "coset correct means" on all groups is equivalent to the Hahn-Banach Theorem, as well as to the existence of invariant means on abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Armando Martino, Motiejus Valiunas

item.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.39033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichm\"uller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Corso

item.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given.
item.dc:creator: G. Militaru

item.title: Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.39345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups. For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time. On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny. For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement. An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.
item.dc:creator: Yinghan Zhang

item.title: Inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-Selfless Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless groups and study their structural properties. We prove a Fourier coefficient extraction theorem for invariant subalgebras of crossed products by such groups under a compatibility assumption on the action. Consequently, every inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless group has the relative $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property, and every finite product of such groups has the $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property. We also introduce another group-theoretic notion, which we call cyclic Powers property. This implies inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, complete $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, and the Powers property, among others. We establish it for groups admitting a topologically free extreme boundary action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points, and for Zariski-dense discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb K)$ containing a biproximal element, where $\mathbb K$ is a local field and $d\geq2$. In particular, we obtain the Powers property for $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb Z)$, $d\geq3$, answering a question posed more than twenty years ago by Bridson-de la Harpe. Finally, we show that every non-trivial mixed identity-free discrete group has the relative invariant subalgebra rigidity property for its group von Neumann algebra. This shows that the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ with $|m|,|n|\geq2$ and $|m|\ne|n|$ have the relative ISR property, thereby answering a question of Dudko-Jiang.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Mario Klisse, Matteo Pagliero

item.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.
item.dc:creator: Jackson Young

item.title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a graph $G$, does it have quantum symmetries, or in other words, is the algebra of the quantum automorphism group non-commutative? In the world of ordinary groups, determining whether a finitely presented group is commutative is undecidable. This is an immediate consequence of the Adian-Rabin theorem, which shows that many natural properties of finitely presented groups are undecidable. In this paper, we prove an Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs, showing that many natural properties of the quantum automorphism group of a graph (including having quantum symmetries) are undecidable. We also show that it's undecidable to determine if the discrete quantum automorphism group is non-trivial. Our methods are based on solution groups of linear system nonlocal games, and we also prove an Adian-Rabin theorem in this context.
item.dc:creator: Josse van Dobben de Bruyn, William Slofstra

item.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2310.08283v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.
item.dc:creator: Milana Golich, D. B. McReynolds

item.title: Minimal doubling for small subsets in compact Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2401.14062v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an asymptotically sharp bound for the minimal doubling of a small measurable subset of a compact connected Lie group, settling a conjecture of Breuillard and Green. Namely, let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of positive dimension $d_G$ with Haar probability measure $\mu_G$, and let $\epsilon > 0$. We show that for all compact subsets $A$ of sufficiently small measure we have \[\mu_G(A^2) \geq \left(2^{d_G-d_M} - \epsilon\right)\mu_G(A),\] where $d_M$ is the maximal dimension of a proper closed subgroup. This recovers, by a different method, the small-measure doubling theorem of Jing--Tran--Zhang for $G=\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathbb{R})$. More generally, for every $\epsilon>0$ and any pair of non-empty compact subsets $A,B$ of sufficiently small measure, we prove the Brunn--Minkowski-type inequality: \[ \mu_G(AB)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}} \geq (1-\epsilon)\left( \mu_G(A)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}} + \mu_G(B)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}}\right).\] We also prove an inverse theorem in the semi-simple case: for any fixed $K\geq1$ and $\delta>0$, every compact $K$-approximate subgroup of sufficiently small positive Haar measure is covered by $C(d_G,K)$ translates of the $\delta$-neighbourhood of a proper closed connected subgroup. Our approach combines this inverse theorem with optimal transport and its recent applications to the Brunn--Minkowski inequality.
item.dc:creator: Simon Machado

item.title: On the complexity of epimorphism testing with virtually abelian targets
item.description: arXiv:2501.05283v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Friedl and L\"oh (2021, Confl. Math.) prove that testing whether or not there is an epimorphism from a finitely presented group to the direct product of an abelian and a finite group, or to a virtually cyclic group, is decidable. Here we prove that these problems are $\mathsf{NP}$-complete. In addition, we show that testing epimorphism is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete when the target is is the semi-direct product of a finitely generated free-abelian group and a finite group which factors through $\{\pm\text{Id}\}$, thus extending the class of virtually abelian target groups for which decidability of epimorphism is known.
item.dc:creator: Murray Elder, Jerry Shen, Armin Wei{\ss}

item.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2508.10394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_{\Gamma}/Z(A_{\Gamma})$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.
item.dc:creator: Kaitlin Ragosta

item.title: A family of accumulation points of non-free rational numbers
item.description: arXiv:2511.10422v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any $q\in\mathbb R$, let $A:=\big(\begin{smallmatrix}1 & 1\\0 & 1\end{smallmatrix}\big), B_q:=\big(\begin{smallmatrix}1 & 0\\q & 1\end{smallmatrix}\big)$ and let $G_q:=\langle A,B_q\rangle\leqslant\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Kim and Koberda conjecture that for every $q\in\mathbb{Q}\cap(-4,4)$, the group $G_q$ is not freely generated by these two matrices. We generalize work of Smilga and construct families of $q$ satisfying the conjecture that accumulate at infinitely many different points in $(-4,4)$. We give different constructions of such families, the first coming from applying tools in Diophantine geometry to certain polynomials arising in Smilga's work, the second from sums of geometric series and the last from ratios of Pell and half-companion Pell numbers accumulating at $1+\sqrt{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Buyalos, Jayden Thadani, Xinbei Wang, Bradley Zykoski, Michael Zshornack

item.title: Irreducible groups and ergodicity in the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2512.12141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if $G$ is a real semi-simple Lie group, and $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of $G$ containing a subgroup $\Sigma$ acting ergodically (in a strong sense) on the Furstenberg boundary of $G$, then $\Gamma$ is not isomorphic to a free product of $\Sigma$ with $\mathbb{Z}$. Moreover, if $\Sigma$ has algebraic entries, then $\Gamma$ has algebraic entries as well. As a consequence, we show that if all irreducible discrete subgroups of ${\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ act ergodically on $\mathbb{S}^1\times \mathbb{S}^1 $, such groups cannot be free groups (or even Gromov hyperbolic). In the appendix, we discuss a connection between the existence of discrete irreducible groups and diophantine properties of Lie groups.
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Dey, Sebastian Hurtado

item.title: Which $F_3$-by-$\mathbb{Z}$s are CAT(0)?
item.description: arXiv:2602.08759v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we point out a mistake in theorem 4.4 of [Sam06], which states that a semidirect product $F_3\rtimes_\phi\mathbb{Z}$ whose defining automorphism $\phi$ is triangular polynomially-growing and fixes a free factor of rank $2$ is a CAT(0) group. We give and prove the corrected statement: such a group is CAT(0), if and only if $\phi$ is the identity or if the element of $F_2$ twisting the non-fixed generator is not in the commutator subgroup of $F_2$. This gives new examples of free-by-cyclic groups that cannot act properly by semisimple isometries on a CAT(0) space, that are similar to Gersten's examples [Ger94]. Some of them, interestingly, are still hierarchically hyperbolic. We also construct CAT(0) structures for new examples of $F_3$-by-$\mathbb{Z}$s by thickening the strips in Bridson's tree of spaces construction [BH99].
item.dc:creator: Leo Delage

item.title: Cohomological and quasi-isometric diversity of groups with property $R_\infty$
item.description: arXiv:2602.17411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How rich is the collection of groups with a given prominent property? In this work we approach this question for property~$R_\infty$, which says that every automorphism $\varphi$ of a given group has infinitely many orbits under the $\varphi$-twisted conjugation action $(g,x) \mapsto gx\varphi(g)^{-1}$. Generalising the soluble groups of Herbert Abels to a large family over many integral domains, we prove that most such groups have property~$R_\infty$ drawing from a classical result of Levchuk and a swift observation by Jabara. Within the broad programme of cataloguing finitely generated groups up to quasi-isometry, our groups can then be separated by finiteness properties and cohomological dimension whilst having~$R_\infty$. Abandoning finite presentability, we establish that property~$R_\infty$ is very abundant in a strong sense: there are uncountably many finitely generated groups (which can all be chosen to be amenable or non-amenable) that have~$R_\infty$ and are pairwise not quasi-isometric. The proofs vary in flavour. On the amenable side we use carefully constructed quotients of Abels' groups and a general strategy for quasi-isometric diversity established by Minasyan, Osin, and Witzel. For the non-amenable constructions we rely on modifications of Leary's type $\mathtt{FP}$ groups, further cohomological arguments, and recent powerful criteria for~$R_\infty$ due to Iveson, Martino, Sgobbi, Wong, and Fournier-Facio.
item.dc:creator: Karel Dekimpe, Paula M. Lins de Araujo, Yuri Santos Rego

item.title: From branching quasiflats to flats in CAT(0) cube complexes
item.description: arXiv:2605.10248v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quasiisometric embeddings between finite-dimensional CAT(0) cube complexes. More specifically, we introduce geometric branching conditions under which flats in the domain, not necessarily of top rank, are mapped within finite Hausdorff distance of flats. As a consequence, one obtains embeddings between natural graphs associated with the Tits boundaries of those cube complexes. These results form a key step in understanding quasiisometric embeddings between right-angled Artin groups. In an appendix, we also explain how the same methods recover previously established rigidity results for quasiisometric embeddings of symmetric spaces and Euclidean buildings of the same spherical type.
item.dc:creator: Shaked Bader, Oussama Bensaid, Harry Petyt

item.title: Quasiisometric embeddings between right-angled Artin groups: rigidity
item.dc:creator: Shaked Bader, Oussama Bensaid, Harry Petyt

item.title: Quasiisometric embeddings between right-angled Artin groups: flexibility
item.description: arXiv:2605.13314v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a complete characterisation of when the right-angled Artin group on one cycle graph can be quasiisometrically embedded in the right-angled Artin group on another cycle graph. In particular, we find infinitely many instances of quasiisometric embeddings where there is no subgroup relation. This contrasts with the fact that such groups are quasiisometrically rigid. More generally, we construct quasiisometric embeddings between graph products of finite or cyclic groups whose underlying graphs are cycles. As a special case, we obtain exotic quasiisometric embeddings of the hyperbolic plane in all right-angled Artin groups whose defining graph contains an induced cycle of length greater than four.
item.dc:creator: Shaked Bader, Oussama Bensaid, Harry Petyt

item.title: A simple acylindrical recipe for non-split characteristic $2$ sharply $k$-transitive actions and their generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2608.10114v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a fairly simple list of conditions on a group $G$ acting acylindrically on a $\delta$-hyperbolic metric space sufficient for the group to admit an action on a set that is $k$-sharp, transitive on $k$-sets and has the property that for any $k$-set $A$ the setwise stabilizer of $A$ acts on $A$ as prescribed by some fixed subgroup of the group of permutations of $k$ elements. In particular, this yields a large class of non-split sharply $2$ and $3$-transitive actions containing many finitely presented groups, and allows us to characterize sharp $2$-transitivity within the class of hyperbolic groups that do not contain a copy of $C_{2}\times C_{2}$.
item.dc:creator: J de la Nuez Gonzalez

item.title: Lie methods for countably categorical Engel groups: the Wilson conjecture for 4-Engel 5-groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.15664v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We are interested in the following conjecture of Wilson from 1981: every locally nilpotent countably categorical group is nilpotent. Following our previous work on the Lie algebra analogue of the conjecture, we use Lie methods to deduce the first nontrivial cases of the Wilson conjecture for n-Engel groups: countably categorical 3-Engel groups and 4-Engel 5-groups are nilpotent, from which we also conclude that countably categorical 4-Engel groups of odd exponent are nilpotent. This is implemented via an exceptional case of the Lazard correspondence, checked using computer algebra systems. We also study the transfer of nilpotency results between the three categories: groups, Lie algebras, associative algebras. Among other things, we prove that the Wilson conjecture implies the analogous nilpotency statement for associative algebras (modulo the commutative case).
item.dc:creator: Christian d'Elb\'ee

item.title: Algebraic and measurable embeddings between square-free right-angled Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.15733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma,\Delta$ be finite simplicial graphs, and assume that $\Gamma$ has no induced squares. We prove that the right-angled Artin group $A(\Delta)$ measurably embeds into $A(\Gamma)$ if and only if $A(\Delta)$ embeds as a subgroup in a graph product of free abelian groups over $\Gamma$. This in turn has a graph-theoretical characterisation which can be checked algorithmically. If additionally $A(\Gamma)$ and $A(\Delta)$ have cohomological dimension equal to two and $A(\Gamma)$ is not isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}\times F_n$, we get that $A(\Delta)$ measurably embeds into $A(\Gamma)$ if and only if it embeds as a subgroup in $A(\Gamma)$. Our proof relies on the following algebraic statement. Let $K_1,\dots,K_n$ be a family of pairwise disjoint cliques in the square-free graph $\Gamma$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_n$ be elements of $A(\Gamma)$ with respective parabolic supports $A(K_1),\dots,A(K_n)$. Then the subgroup of $A(\Gamma)$ generated by $g_1,\dots,g_n$ is a right-angled Artin group, where the only relations impose that $g_i$ and $g_j$ commute if $K_i\cup K_j$ is contained in a clique of $\Gamma$. The same holds true more generally for pairwise disjoint cliques $K_1,\dots,K_n$ in the extension graph $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ext}}$, up to possibly replacing the elements $g_i$ by powers.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Abgrall, Alexandra Gurieva, Camille Horbez

item.title: Smallest quotients and profinite rigidity of irreducible spherical type Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.25940v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that irreducible spherical type Artin groups are profinitely rigid within the class of all spherical type Artin groups. As part of the proof, building on ideas of Kolay for the $n$-strand braid group, we compute the smallest non-abelian quotient of every spherical type Artin group. In particular, given an irreducible spherical type Artin group, its smallest non-abelian quotient is always that of the corresponding Coxeter group, except for dihedral Artin groups of weight divisible by $4$, which all have $\mathfrak S_3$ as a non-abelian quotient. Parts of the proof also rely on the computation of the cohomological dimension of the profinite completion of certain Artin groups.
item.dc:creator: Federica Gavazzi, Igor Haladjian, Luis Paris

item.title: The small index property of automorphism groups of ab-initio generic structures
item.description: arXiv:1510.00586v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose $M$ is a countable ab-initio (uncollapsed) generic structure which is obtained from a pre-dimension function with rational coefficients. We show that if $H$ is a subgroup of $\mbox{Aut}\left(M\right)$ with $\left[\mbox{Aut}\left(M\right):H\right]<2^{\aleph_{0}}$, then there exists a finite set $A\subseteq M$ such that $\mbox{Aut}_{A}\left(M\right)\subseteq H$. This shows that $\mbox{Aut}\left(M\right)$ has the small index property.
item.dc:creator: Zaniar Ghadernezhad

item.title: Topology of irregular isomonodromy times on a fixed pointed curve
item.description: arXiv:2208.02575v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We will define and study (moduli) spaces of deformations of irregular classes on Riemann surfaces, which provide an intrinsic viewpoint on the `times' of irregular isomonodromy systems in general. Our aim is to study the deeper generalisation of the G-braid groups that occur as fundamental groups of such deformation spaces, with particular focus on the generalisation of the full G-braid groups.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot, Gabriele Rembado

item.title: On the source algebra equivalence class of blocks with cyclic defect groups, II
item.description: arXiv:2502.09176v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This series of papers is a contribution to the program of classifying $p$-blocks of finite groups up to source algebra equivalence, starting with the case of cyclic blocks. To any $p$-block $\mathbf{B}$ of a finite group with cyclic defect group $D$, Linckelmann associated an invariant $W( \mathbf{B} )$, which is an indecomposable endo-permutation module over $D$, and which, together with the Brauer tree of $\mathbf{B}$, essentially determines its source algebra equivalence class. In Parts II-IV of our series of papers, we classify, for odd $p$, those endo-permutation modules of cyclic $p$-groups arising from $p$-blocks of quasisimple groups. In the present Part II, we reduce the desired classification for the quasisimple classical groups of Lie type $B$, $C$, and $D$ to the corresponding objective for the general linear and unitary groups; the classification is completed for the latter groups.
item.dc:creator: Gerhard Hiss, Caroline Lassueur

item.title: An upper bound for the list-distinguishing chromatic number of $K_{r,r+1}$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.11992v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 2006, Collins and Trenk obtained a general sharp upper bound for the distinguishing chromatic number of a connected graph. Inspired by Catlin's combinatorial techniques from 1978, we establish improved upper bounds for classes of connected graphs that have only small complete bigraphs as induced subgraphs. In this framework, we also consider the list-distinguishing chromatic number of such graphs. We apply Menger's theorem to demonstrate applications of our main result for graphs whose constructions are based on Paley graphs and Cayley graphs on Dihedral groups.
item.dc:creator: Amitayu Banerjee

item.title: Quasi-conformal VS quasi-isometric equivalence in spaces with controlled growth
item.description: arXiv:2510.12161v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study conditions under which quasi-conformal homeomorphisms are quasi-isometries. We show that if two nilpotent geodesic Lie groups are quasi-conformally homeomorphic, then they are quasi-isometrically equivalent. We also give more general results beyond the nilpotent case. In particular, we show that quasi-conformal homeomorphisms between geodesic Lie groups are quasi-isometries whenever the spaces have strict parabolic or hyperbolic conformal type. As a consequence, quasi-conformal homeomorphisms between geodesic Lie groups with infinite fundamental group are quasi-isometries. The statements for Lie groups are deduced from a more general study on metric measure spaces with uniformly locally bounded geometry.
item.dc:creator: Katrin F\"assler, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo, Alessandro Ottazzi, Pierre Pansu

item.title: Property (T) group factors whose Jones index set equals all positive integers
item.description: arXiv:2511.04822v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using a m\'elange of techniques at the rich intersection of deformation/rigidity theory, finite index subfactor theory, and geometric group theory, we prove the existence of a continuum of property (T) factors that are pairwise non-stably isomorphic and whose Jones index sets consist of all positive integers. These factors are realized as group von Neumann algebras $\mathcal{L}(G)$ associated with property (T) generalized wreath-like product groups $G \in \mathscr{WR}(A, B \curvearrowright I)$ introduced in [CIOS23b], where $A$ is abelian, $B$ is a non-parabolic subgroup of a relatively hyperbolic group with residually finite peripheral structure, and $B \curvearrowright I$ is a faithful action with infinite orbits. Integer index subfactors of $\mathcal{L}(G)$ are constructed from extensions of $G$. This result advances an open question of P. de la Harpe [dlH95].
item.dc:creator: Ionut Chifan, Junhwi Lim

item.title: The asymptotic size of finite irreducible semigroups of rational matrices
item.description: arXiv:2601.01236v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate the maximum size of finite semigroups of rational $n \times n$ matrices, with the goal of shedding more light on their structure. Such semigroups provide a rich generalisation of transition monoids of unambiguous (and, in particular, deterministic) finite automata. While in general such semigroups can be arbitrarily large in terms of $n$, a classical result of Sch\"utzenberger from 1962 implies an upper bound of $2^{O(n^2 \log n)}$ for irreducible semigroups. A semigroup of rational matrices is called irreducible if the only subspaces of $\mathbb{Q}^n$ that are invariant for all matrices in the semigroup are $\mathbb{Q}^n$ and the subspace consisting only of the zero vector. Irreducible matrix semigroups can be viewed as the building blocks of general matrix semigroups, and as such play an important role in mathematics and computer science. From the point of view of automata theory, they can be seen as a generalisation of strongly connected weighted automata. Using a very different technique from that of Sch\"utzenberger, we improve the upper bound on the cardinality to $3^{n^2}$. This is the main result of the paper. The bound is in some sense tight, as we show that there exists, for every $n$, a finite irreducible semigroup with $3^{\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor}$ rational matrices. Our main result also leads to an improvement of a bound, due to Almeida and Steinberg, on the mortality threshold of finite semigroups of rational matrices. The mortality threshold is a number $\ell$ such that if the zero matrix is in the semigroup, then the zero matrix can be written as a product of at most $\ell$ matrices from any subset that generates the semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Kiefer, Andrew Ryzhikov

item.title: Equilateral Completion in Floretion Triangular Coordinates: Locality, Product Points, and Reflection Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2608.15925v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study nondegenerate equilateral triangles whose vertices are centroids of the $4^n$ order-$n$ floretion tiles. Scaled integer triangular coordinates give exact equilateral completions and, by an obstruction modulo $3$, show that all three vertices have the same tile orientation. In particular, the complete triangle family and its synchronized local cyclic subfamily have respective sizes $|E_n|=\frac{4^n(4^n-1)}{12},\quad |L_n|=\frac{7^n-4^n}{3},$ so the local proportion tends to zero. Our principal new result answers the radial-homogeneity question left open in the preceding revision: for every order, the number of triangles containing a given tile is given by an exact affine formula in its squared scaled centroid radius. Although the two tile orientations have different formulas, their attainable squared radii belong to disjoint residue classes modulo $3$, yielding a single radial-incidence law on the full centroid set. We also determine local and nonlocal vertex incidences and obtain circular-shell and squared-radius moment identities. The unsigned vertex product defines an algebraic product point. By a rigidity theorem of Ma and Zhang, the multiplication-generated triangles are precisely the nontrivial global cyclic orbits; combining this with our geometric shell classification, we show that the product point is the origin exactly when the Euclidean triangle center is the origin. Further results enumerate central-vertex, no-$e$, and main-axis families, derive Fibonacci and finite-state recurrences for product-centered and reflection-restricted classes, and characterize pairwise anticommutation.
item.dc:creator: Creighton Dement

item.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia V. Ferrer, Salvador Hern\'andez, Isabel Sep\'ulveda
